cultural.vision_reason: Studio portrait of a Missouri chief, a Métis/French interpreter, and Little Pipe, an Otoe chief, the latter wearing feathered headdress, peace medal, blanket, leggings and moccasins and holding a tomahawk — a documentary photo showing authentic Otoe dress alongside related Missouri regalia.

physical.title: photographic print (black and white); album
physical.summary:
Photograph (black and white) from an album; studio portrait of three men, Something Eaten Raw (Wathake Ruche) a Missouri Chief;  Baptiste Barnabi, and interpreter; and Little Pipe (Ranunwe Inge), an Otoe Chief, all three seated;  Both the Missouri Chief and Little Pipe wear headdresses with eagle feathers, necklaces, a peace medal, checked cloth shirts, wool blankets around their waists, leggings and moccasins, and both holding tomahawks; Baptiste Barnabi wears a tie, shirt, vest, suit jacket, trousers and leather shoes; Washington, D.C, USA. 
Albumen print
